examples.title: Tell "port unreachable" from "key rejected"
examples.goal: The external panel cannot connect, and both cases look like a timeout.
examples.result: From the machine running the panel: `curl http://<ip>:8080/api/ping`. A 200 with `{"success":true,"mod":"neoessentials","mode":"..."}` means HTTP is alive — next, check pairing/the API key. Connection refused means a firewall, the bind address, or the dashboard did not start. `/dashboard status` in game shows whether the built-in HTTP server is up.

examples.title: API only, without the built-in UI
examples.goal: You run the Laravel NeoEssentials-Dashboard, do not need the built-in page on :8080, and it spams the log about a missing index.html.
examples.result: `webDashboard.mode: "external"` (the default) registers only `/api/*`. Changing the mode requires a restart. `internal` and `both` also serve the UI bundle at `/` — for that the UI must be packaged into the jar.

edgeCases.title: mode is read at startup
edgeCases.body: Like modules, `webDashboard.mode` does not change on `/neoe reload`. GET `/api/ping` needs no authorization and is registered in every mode — it is the probe for "is the port alive".
edgeCases.fix: Changed the mode — restart. Diagnose the network with ping, not by logging in to the panel.

knownIssues.title: On old builds /dashboard start was dead code
knownIssues.body: The class existed but was not registered in the dispatcher — the command was "unknown". In this branch /dashboard is wired up; if the server runs an ancient jar, status/start will be unknown regardless of the config.
knownIssues.fix: Check the mod version. On the current fork the command should appear in /help when the module is enabled.
